title: Impact of Bond Downgrade on Equity CAR

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

We will use an Event Study approach to estimate the impact of bond credit rating downgrades on a company's equity cumulative abnormal returns (CAR). This method is suitable because it allows us to measure the stock's performance relative to a benchmark (market returns) around the event window. The key assumption is that the stock returns are not systematically different from the market returns in the absence of the event.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(plm)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s56_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns (AR) by subtracting market returns from stock returns
data$ar <- data$ret - data$mkt_ret

# Define the event window (-10 to 0) and estimation window (-11 to -1)
event_window <- c(-10, 0)
estimation_window <- c(-11, -1)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window
data$car <- ave(data$ar, data$stock_id, FUN = function(x) {
  mean(x[(x$event_day >= event_window[1]) & (x$event_day <= event_window[2])])
})

# Calculate the average CAR across all stocks
avg_car <- mean(data$car, na.rm = TRUE)

# Print the average CAR
print(avg_car)

# Robustness check: Calculate CAR for different event windows
event_windows <- list(c(-10, 0), c(-5, 0), c(0, 5))
for (window in event_windows) {
  data$car <- ave(data$ar, data$stock_id, FUN = function(x) {
    mean(x[(x$event_day >= window[1]) & (x$event_day <= window[2])])
  })
  avg_car <- mean(data$car, na.rm = TRUE)
  print(paste("Average CAR for window", window[1], ":", window[2], ":", avg_car))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

We expect the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) to be negative around the event of a bond credit rating downgrade. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the severity of the downgrade and the market's perception of the company's financial health. A more severe downgrade is likely to result in a larger negative impact on equity performance. The exact magnitude is difficult to predict without more information about the specific downgrades and companies involved, but we expect a statistically significant negative effect.
